files.purpose: Status M. MCPOAuth implements the whole OAuth 2.1 + PKCE sign-in for remote MCP servers: protected-resource discovery from the 401 WWW-Authenticate challenge or two well-known paths, authorization-server metadata at up to four candidate URLs, dynamic client registration as "Droppy Code", a loopback callback listener on 127.0.0.1:<any>/callback with a 300 s timeout and branded HTML pages, the code exchange, and refresh with a per-server single-flight gate, storing sessions under Keychain field "oauth" and clients under "oauth-client". The B2->B3 change is in postForm (:768-788): the application/x-www-form-urlencoded body is no longer URLComponents.percentEncodedQuery over URLQueryItems but `name=value` pairs joined by '&' where both name and value go through the new private formEncode(_:) (:790-793), which percent-encodes every character outside A-Z a-z 0-9 - . _ ~.

feature_notes: B2->B3 behaviour change in postForm: B2 set `components.queryItems = fields.map { URLQueryItem(...) }` and sent `components.percentEncodedQuery ?? ""` (B2 :772-773, :778), i.e. URLComponents query encoding, which leaves characters such as '+', '/', ':' and '?' unescaped. B3 sends `fields.map { "\(formEncode($0.0))=\(formEncode($0.1))" }.joined(separator: "&")` (:776) with formEncode allowing only A-Z a-z 0-9 - . _ ~ (:790-793). Wire effect: a '+' in a code, refresh token, client secret or verifier is now sent as %2B (a form decoder no longer turns it into a space), and redirect_uri/resource URLs now arrive as e.g. http%3A%2F%2F127.0.0.1%3A<port>%2Fcallback. Field order is unchanged. It affects both exchangeCode (:622) and performRefresh (:661).
formEncode falls back to the unencoded value when addingPercentEncoding returns nil (:792).

Line shifts: :1-771 unchanged; B2 :774-791 -> :772-789 (-2); B2 :792 onward -> +3 (oauthErrorMessage B2 :792-798 -> :795-801, origin B2 :800-812 -> :803-815, PKCE helpers B2 :816-834 -> :819-837, success/failure pages B2 :838-852 -> :841-855, page B2 :854-913 -> :857-916, logo line B2 :904 -> :907, wordmark B2 :907 -> :910, self-close script B2 :909 -> :912, escapeHTML B2 :915-929 -> :918-932).

unresolved_questions: Exact hex case of formEncode's escapes is Foundation runtime behaviour (addingPercentEncoding is expected to emit uppercase hex such as %2F); the pinned source does not state it and it was not observed on a reference macOS runtime in this read. The port fixture should pin whatever the reference produces.

files.purpose: Status M, one dead function removed. files.purpose: Status M. MCPProxy is the loopback HTTP relay at http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp/<server id> that providers are pointed at for OAuth servers: it persists its port in mcp/proxy-port (kernel-picked, repicked once on a bind failure), parses a request head up to 65536 bytes and a Content-Length body up to 32 MiB, forwards five client headers plus the route's headers and a fresh bearer token upstream with a 3600 s timeout, replays once on an upstream 401, and writes back Content-Type, Mcp-Session-Id and Cache-Control. B3 changes two things: the four print(...) diagnostics became os Logger calls (subsystem "iordv.droppycode", category "mcp-proxy", :7) without the "MCPProxy: " prefix, and the text/event-stream relay now buffers bytes and emits one hex-sized chunk per line (at each '\n', plus a final remainder) through the new chunk(_:) helper instead of one 1-byte chunk per byte.

Nothing goes to standard output any more; the lines lose the "MCPProxy: " prefix and gain a level (error/info) and a category.

B2->B3 SSE relay (:378-389): B2 sent `"1
" + byte + "
"` per byte. B3 appends each byte to `buffer`; when the byte is '
' it sends Self.chunk(buffer) and clears the buffer; after the loop ends normally a non-empty remainder is sent as one more chunk. chunk(_:) frames `String(payload.count, radix: 16) + "
" + payload + "
"` (:413-418), so sizes are lowercase hex. A stream error still ends the relay silently (:390-391) but now DISCARDS any buffered partial line, because the remainder flush (:387-389) is inside the do block; the terminating "0

" is still sent (:392). A partial line (no '
' yet) is held until its newline or the end of the stream.

B2->B3 non-SSE relay: `payload.reserveCapacity(Int(response.expectedContentLength))` when expectedContentLength > 0 (:397-399); a capacity hint only, still a per-byte append loop, no observable change.

Line shifts: +2 from B2 :6 (after the two added lines) through B2 :376; +7 from B2 :382 to :389; +10 from B2 :390 to :402; +17 from B2 :403 to the end (send B2 :403-409 -> :420-426, respond B2 :411-422 -> :428-439, statusHead B2 :424-431 -> :441-448, reasonPhrase B2 :433-450 -> :450-467, jsonError B2 :452-459 -> :469-476).
unresolved_questions: OSLog applies its default privacy to interpolated values (the pinned source sets no privacy: modifiers); under Apple's documented default, non-numeric interpolations such as serverID, error and error.localizedDescription would show as <private> outside a debugger, while the UInt16 port stays visible. This is Apple runtime behaviour, not stated in the pinned source, and was not observed on a reference runtime; ED-163's port Logger writes messages verbatim, so whether the Windows log should redact anything needs a ruling or an explicit note under ED-163.
